post_text:
I almost took the dry-erase marker right out of his hand.

He was pitching a solution that clashed with everything I had spent a decade practicing.

Every instinct screamed at me to interrupt, take over the whiteboard, and steer the room back to familiar territory.

Stepping in would have eased my personal anxiety, but it would have quietly crushed his confidence in front of his peers.

I forced myself to stay silent, grip the edge of the table, and let him carry the vision to the end.

The project ran into serious turbulence a month later, right where I privately suspected it would. Instead of swooping in with an uninvited rescue, I simply asked him how he wanted to navigate the setback.

He rallied the group, untangled the complications, and arrived at an outcome far simpler than anything I would have dictated.

Real mentorship means resisting the urge to duplicate yourself in other people. True leadership is not about preventing every mistake, but absorbing the discomfort of watching someone struggle so they can actually grow. 🤝
lesson_extracted: True leadership requires absorbing the discomfort of watching someone struggle so they can develop genuine ownership.
